items.label: f05-api-fetch-contract
items.front: What does apiFetch guarantee to every hook, and how does it treat a body that is not JSON?
items.back: It sends JSON with cache: "no-store" (React Query is the cache, not the browser's HTTP cache). It parses with json().catch(() => null), so a non-JSON body becomes null rather than a parse error. On a non-2xx status it throws ApiClientError carrying the status, the body's message or "Request failed.", and the whole payload for callers that need details; otherwise it returns the body cast to T.

items.label: f06-create-note-nested-write
items.front: What does creating a note write, and what commits together?
items.back: One nested note.create on the transaction client writes the note, an OWNER collaborator row for the creator and revision 1 ("Initial version"), and returns it with the detail include. The service then writes a NOTE_CREATED audit row on the same transaction client, so note, membership, first revision and audit commit or roll back together. Ownership comes from the session, never from the body.

items.label: f04-session-lifecycle
items.front: Summarize the session lifecycle in Collab Notes.
items.back: 32 random bytes as a hex token; only sha256(token:SESSION_SECRET) is stored; fixed 14-day expiry (lastSeenAt is updated but never extends it); every API request looks the session up and reads the user role; expired rows are never cleaned up, and logout needs a live session.

items.label: f02-404-before-403
items.front: Why does a non-collaborator get 404 while a viewer who tries to share gets 403?
items.back: Reads are scoped by buildAccessibleNoteWhere, so a member who is not a collaborator never sees the note and gets 404 NOTE_NOT_FOUND; they cannot tell "not shared" from "missing". A collaborator can see it, so lacking a capability is reported as 403.

items.label: f07-conflict-response-contract
items.front: What does a 409 VERSION_CONFLICT response body contain, and which type describes it?
items.back: apiError's envelope { error: "VERSION_CONFLICT", message, details }, where details is { latestNote: { id, title, currentBody, currentVersionNumber, updatedAt, lastEditedAt, status } } from buildConflictDetails. The ConflictPayload type in types/note.ts describes a flat shape with latestNote at the top level, and nothing imports it; the workspace reads details.latestNote through its own local type.

items.label: f01-access-level
items.front: What does getNoteAccessLevel return for an EDITOR on an ACTIVE note, and for any collaborator on an ARCHIVED note?
items.back: EDITOR on ACTIVE: canEdit true, canManageSharing false, canArchive false. On ARCHIVED, canEdit is false for everyone (admins too), while canManageSharing and canArchive keep their values. A member with no collaborator row gets 404 NOTE_NOT_FOUND.

items.label: f08-filtered-include-permission
items.front: How does each sidebar row get the caller's own permission without loading every collaborator?
items.back: The list include filters the collaborators relation to where: { userId: sessionUserId } and selects only userId and permission, so each note brings at most the caller's row. toSummaryDto reads collaborators[0]?.permission. An APP_ADMIN often has no row; the fallback is ownerId ? "OWNER" : "VIEWER", and since ownerId is always set, admins see OWNER.

items.label: f03-save-protection
items.front: How is a note save protected against concurrent edits?
items.back: A pre-check compares currentVersionNumber with baseVersionNumber (409 VERSION_CONFLICT plus a NOTE_CONFLICT_REJECTED audit). Inside the transaction a conditional updateMany on the expected version, backed by @@unique([noteId, versionNumber]), catches the race; losing it also returns 409, but without an audit row.

items.prompt: A co-owner (a collaborator row with OWNER, not the Note.ownerId user) tries to set the Note.ownerId user to EDITOR. What happens?

choices.text: 403 FORBIDDEN, as only the Note.ownerId user may manage sharing
409, as a note must keep more than one OWNER row on it
422 INVALID_PERMISSION_CHANGE, and the ownerId user keeps OWNER
It is accepted, as co-owners may change any collaborator

choices: 403 FORBIDDEN, as only the Note.ownerId user may manage sharing
409, as a note must keep more than one OWNER row on it
422 INVALID_PERMISSION_CHANGE, and the ownerId user keeps OWNER
It is accepted, as co-owners may change any collaborator

items.explanation: Co-owners pass assertCanManageSharing, but upsertCollaborator refuses any non-OWNER permission for the user whose id is note.ownerId.

items.prompt: A user whose session row has expired clicks a raw POST /api/auth/logout. What happens to their cookie?

choices.text: It is cleared, and the expired session row is deleted as well
It stays: withAuth returns 401 before the handler clears it
It stays, but the expired session row is deleted by the call
It is cleared, as logout works even for a stale session

choices: It is cleared, and the expired session row is deleted as well
It stays: withAuth returns 401 before the handler clears it
It stays, but the expired session row is deleted by the call
It is cleared, as logout works even for a stale session

items.explanation: withAuth resolves no session and returns 401 UNAUTHENTICATED without calling the handler, so clearSessionCookie never runs (finding F9).

items.prompt: A note has 500 revisions. A user opens it in the workspace. Where do the entries in the Version history panel come from, and how many are there?

choices.text: All 500, from the revisions route; the detail's 8 go unused
The newest 8, from the revisions route's take of eight
All 500, from the detail, which embeds the whole revision history
The newest 8, from the revisions embedded in the detail

choices: All 500, from the revisions route; the detail's 8 go unused
The newest 8, from the revisions route's take of eight
All 500, from the detail, which embeds the whole revision history
The newest 8, from the revisions embedded in the detail

items.explanation: The detail include embeds revisions with take: 8, newest first (note-repository.ts:60-64), and every detail response carries them. The panel never reads them: the workspace passes revisionsQuery.data (notes-workspace.tsx:267-270), which comes from GET /api/notes/:id/revisions, and listAccessibleRevisions there has no take at all (note-repository.ts:110-128). So opening the note loads eight revisions nobody shows plus all 500 that the panel renders, and both payloads grow with the history. A cursor-paginated revisions route, with the detail dropping its embedded copy, would bound both.

items.prompt: A save passes the baseVersionNumber pre-check, but the conditional update then matches zero rows because another save won. What happens?

choices.text: 409 VERSION_CONFLICT, with no conflict audit row written
200, as the pre-check already passed, so the save is applied
500, as the transaction fails when the update matches nothing
409 VERSION_CONFLICT, and NOTE_CONFLICT_REJECTED is audited

choices: 409 VERSION_CONFLICT, with no conflict audit row written
200, as the pre-check already passed, so the save is applied
500, as the transaction fails when the update matches nothing
409 VERSION_CONFLICT, and NOTE_CONFLICT_REJECTED is audited

items.explanation: Only the pre-check path writes NOTE_CONFLICT_REJECTED. In the race path the transaction returns null and the service throws the same 409 without any audit call (finding F3).

items.prompt: A user's session row expires while /notes stays open. They click a note they have not opened in this tab. What do they see?

choices.text: A redirect to /login, from the notes page's server-side session check
The Choose a note panel, with nothing redirecting to /login
A 401 message in the editor's banner, from the hook
The note's text, served from cache until staleTime ends

choices: A redirect to /login, from the notes page's server-side session check
The Choose a note panel, with nothing redirecting to /login
A 401 message in the editor's banner, from the hook
The note's text, served from cache until staleTime ends

items.explanation: The /notes page is a server component that checks the session and redirects only while it renders (page.tsx:13-19). After that, data comes from React Query in the client. The new note's detail request reaches withAuth, which answers 401 UNAUTHENTICATED as JSON (with-auth.ts:32-41); apiFetch throws, the query errors and its data stays undefined, and the workspace renders the editor only when noteQuery.data exists, otherwise the Choose a note to start editing panel (notes-workspace.tsx:182-256). No code reads a query error or reacts to 401, so nothing navigates. A note never opened in this tab has no cached data, and the editor banner shows only messages that save, create and status handlers set.

items.prompt: A signed-in user POSTs to /api/notes with the body {not json. Which status comes back?

choices.text: 400, as invalid JSON is the classic bad request status for it
422 VALIDATION_ERROR, as parseSchema rejects the body payload
500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, as the parse error is not an AppError
401, as an unreadable body is treated as an unauthenticated call

choices: 400, as invalid JSON is the classic bad request status for it
422 VALIDATION_ERROR, as parseSchema rejects the body payload
500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, as the parse error is not an AppError
401, as an unreadable body is treated as an unauthenticated call

items.explanation: request.json() throws a SyntaxError before parseSchema runs; apiError maps only AppError instances, so everything else becomes 500 (finding F1).

items.prompt: The note owner shares an ARCHIVED note with a teammate as VIEWER. What happens?

choices.text: The share is accepted and audited, though the note is archived
422, as only an OWNER grant is allowed on an archived note
403, as archiving removes the capabilities of the note owner
409 NOTE_ARCHIVED, as the note must be restored before sharing

choices: The share is accepted and audited, though the note is archived
422, as only an OWNER grant is allowed on an archived note
403, as archiving removes the capabilities of the note owner
409 NOTE_ARCHIVED, as the note must be restored before sharing

items.explanation: Archiving clears canEdit, but canManageSharing stays isOwner, and assertCanManageSharing does not look at the status. The design doc records this as a partial transition guard (check S6).

items.prompt: A co-owner (OWNER row, not Note.ownerId) grants OWNER to an existing EDITOR. What happens?

choices.text: 422, as OWNER is not an accepted value in shareNoteSchema
It is accepted and audited, making the editor a co-owner
403, as only the Note.ownerId user may grant OWNER rights
It is accepted, but the new co-owner cannot change status

choices: 422, as OWNER is not an accepted value in shareNoteSchema
It is accepted and audited, making the editor a co-owner
403, as only the Note.ownerId user may grant OWNER rights
It is accepted, but the new co-owner cannot change status

items.explanation: isOwner is true for any OWNER row, so co-owners pass assertCanManageSharing. shareNoteSchema accepts any NotePermission, and the new OWNER row also gets canArchive. This is finding F6.

items.prompt: A VIEWER collaborator sends PUT /api/notes/:id to edit a note that is ARCHIVED. Which response do they get?

choices.text: 404 NOTE_NOT_FOUND, as archived notes are hidden
403 FORBIDDEN, as a viewer row does not carry edit rights
409 NOTE_ARCHIVED, as the archive check runs first
422 VALIDATION_ERROR, as the body is not accepted

choices: 404 NOTE_NOT_FOUND, as archived notes are hidden
403 FORBIDDEN, as a viewer row does not carry edit rights
409 NOTE_ARCHIVED, as the archive check runs first
422 VALIDATION_ERROR, as the body is not accepted

items.explanation: assertCanEditNote tests noteStatus === "ARCHIVED" before canEdit, so even a viewer who could never edit is told to restore the note first.

items.prompt: The sidebar list returns 200 notes, each including its owner and the caller's collaborator row. How many SELECT statements does Prisma send for that one findMany?

choices.text: 401: the notes, then two separate lookups for each one of the notes
Three: notes, then owners and collaborators by IN lists
One: Prisma joins both relations into a single query
201: the notes, then one owner query for every note

choices: 401: the notes, then two separate lookups for each one of the notes
Three: notes, then owners and collaborators by IN lists
One: Prisma joins both relations into a single query
201: the notes, then one owner query for every note

items.explanation: listAccessibleForUser is one findMany with two includes, owner and a collaborators relation filtered to the caller (note-repository.ts:78-100). Prisma's default relation strategy loads each included relation with one extra query that selects by an IN list of the parent keys, so the cost is one query per relation level, not per row. A probe with Prisma 6.19.3 (the lockfile version, no relationJoins preview in the schema) on PostgreSQL 18 logged exactly three SELECTs for 200 notes: Note (with the collaborators-some filter as a subquery), User by id IN (...), and the collaborator rows by note id. An N+1 would appear only if code looped over notes and queried each one.

items.prompt: A developer adds a required wordCount: number field to the NoteDetail type in src/types/note.ts and changes nothing else. Where does tsc report an error?

choices.text: Nowhere, since the type only describes JSON on the wire
In use-notes.ts, where apiFetch is typed with NoteDetail
In the note routes, which hand ok({ note }) the service result
In toDetailDto, the one place that builds a NoteDetail object

choices: Nowhere, since the type only describes JSON on the wire
In use-notes.ts, where apiFetch is typed with NoteDetail
In the note routes, which hand ok({ note }) the service result
In toDetailDto, the one place that builds a NoteDetail object

items.explanation: NoteDetail is shared: the service returns it and the hooks and components consume it. The only code that constructs one is toDetailDto, whose object literal is annotated as NoteDetail (note-service.ts:89-125), so a missing required property is error TS2741 there; a probe with TypeScript 5.9.3 reported exactly that. The hooks only name the type in apiFetch's generic (use-notes.ts:28-35), and apiFetch ends with return data as T (fetcher.ts:44), a cast that checks nothing. The routes hand the service result to ok() without naming the type. So the server side is forced to supply the field, while nothing verifies that the JSON the browser receives has it.

items.prompt: The note owner shares the note with an email address that has no user account yet. Which response does the API return?

choices.text: 200, and a new user is created on the spot with that email
422 VALIDATION_ERROR, as the email is not a registered one
404 USER_NOT_FOUND, as there is no user with that email
201, and a pending invitation is created for that email

choices: 200, and a new user is created on the spot with that email
422 VALIDATION_ERROR, as the email is not a registered one
404 USER_NOT_FOUND, as there is no user with that email
201, and a pending invitation is created for that email

items.explanation: After the sharing check passes, upsertCollaborator looks the email up and throws 404 USER_NOT_FOUND. There is no sign-up route and no invitation model.

items.prompt: With a note open, the owner adds a collaborator. The share hook writes the response into ["notes", id] and then invalidates ["notes"]. Which of that note's queries refetch?

choices.text: Only the detail, as revisions have their own query key
The detail and its revisions, under the shared prefix
Only the revisions, as the detail was written just now
Neither, as only the list has the key ["notes"] itself

choices: Only the detail, as revisions have their own query key
The detail and its revisions, under the shared prefix
Only the revisions, as the detail was written just now
Neither, as only the list has the key ["notes"] itself

items.explanation: The key factory nests every note query under one root: all is ["notes"], detail is ["notes", id] and revisions is ["notes", id, "revisions"] (use-notes.ts:15-19). invalidateQueries matches by prefix, so invalidating ["notes"] (use-notes.ts:107-110) marks the list, the detail and the revisions stale and refetches every one that is mounted. A probe with @tanstack/query-core 5.99.0 (the lockfile version) refetched list, detail and revisions after exactly this onSuccess. Writing the response with setQueryData first does not exempt the detail: the invalidation flags it again. So the open note's detail is fetched a second time and its revisions are fetched although sharing never changes them.

items.prompt: A user edits version 5 of a note while a teammate saves version 6. The user's save gets 409 VERSION_CONFLICT with details.latestNote. Nothing has refetched the note. What does the editor show next?

choices.text: A merge of the user's edits into the version 6 text
The user's typed edits, kept under a newer-revision banner
The version 6 text, loaded into the editor from latestNote's data
The cached version 5 text, with the user's typed edits gone

choices: A merge of the user's edits into the version 6 text
The user's typed edits, kept under a newer-revision banner
The version 6 text, loaded into the editor from latestNote's data
The cached version 5 text, with the user's typed edits gone

items.explanation: The conflict branch overwrites the draft with latestNote and sets draft.versionNumber to 6 (notes-workspace.tsx:210-228). The editor shows the draft only while draft.versionNumber equals the cached note's currentVersionNumber (notes-workspace.tsx:74-91), and the cache still holds version 5: the save hook has no onError and nothing in the branch invalidates the detail (use-notes.ts:64-91). So the editor falls back to the cached version 5 title and body. The typed edits were replaced, version 6 is not displayed even though the message says the latest version was reloaded, and with title and body equal to the cached note the editor is not dirty (note-editor.tsx:44). A re-save after typing again still sends base version 5 and is refused again.

items.prompt: User A signs out successfully, and user B signs in from the same tab and lands on /notes. Before B's first list request returns, what does the sidebar show?

choices.text: A's notes, until the list's 15 s staleTime runs out
B's notes, as the server page embeds them in its HTML
A's notes, until the sign-in refetches the list query
No notes yet, as logout emptied the whole query cache

choices: A's notes, until the list's 15 s staleTime runs out
B's notes, as the server page embeds them in its HTML
A's notes, until the sign-in refetches the list query
No notes yet, as logout emptied the whole query cache

items.explanation: One QueryClient lives for the whole tab (app-providers.tsx:15-24), so cached data would survive client-side navigation between users. The logout hook prevents that: its onSuccess awaits queryClient.clear() (use-logout-mutation.ts:15-17), which removes every query, and only then does the workspace push to /login and refresh (notes-workspace.tsx:153-157). A probe with @tanstack/query-core 5.99.0 left zero cached queries after clear(). When B lands on /notes the list query starts empty and shows nothing until its fetch returns. The server page passes only the session to the client component; it does not fetch notes.

items.prompt: An EDITOR collaborator tries to share the note with a teammate through POST /api/notes/:id/share. What happens?

choices.text: 403 FORBIDDEN, as only owners may manage sharing
422, as editors may only send a VIEWER grant
200, as editors may add viewers to a note but not owners
404 USER_NOT_FOUND, before any role is checked

choices: 403 FORBIDDEN, as only owners may manage sharing
422, as editors may only send a VIEWER grant
200, as editors may add viewers to a note but not owners
404 USER_NOT_FOUND, before any role is checked

items.explanation: canManageSharing is isOwner, which is false for an EDITOR row, so assertCanManageSharing throws 403 before the email is even looked up.

items.prompt: A user clicks Create while another note is open. The create succeeds and the workspace selects the new note. Which requests does the browser send for the new note?

choices.text: Its detail and revisions, as a new key always fetches once
Only its detail, as revisions come inside the detail data
Only its revisions, as the hook seeded the new note's detail
None, as the create response seeds detail and revisions

choices: Its detail and revisions, as a new key always fetches once
Only its detail, as revisions come inside the detail data
Only its revisions, as the hook seeded the new note's detail
None, as the create response seeds detail and revisions

items.explanation: onSuccess first awaits the invalidation of ["notes"] and then calls setQueryData for ["notes", newId] with the created note (use-notes.ts:57-60). The workspace awaits mutateAsync and then selects the new id (notes-workspace.tsx:171-178). The new detail query mounts onto fresh seeded data inside its 15 s staleTime, so it does not fetch; its revisions key was never seeded, so that query fetches. A probe with @tanstack/query-core 5.99.0 showed only the revisions fetch for the new note after this sequence.

items.prompt: The note owner sends PATCH /api/notes/:id/status with status ARCHIVED for a note that is already ARCHIVED. What happens?

choices.text: 403, as an archived note can be restored by an admin user alone
200, and a second NOTE_STATUS_CHANGED audit row is written
409 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION, as the note is already archived
422, as ARCHIVED is not a valid target status for the route

choices: 403, as an archived note can be restored by an admin user alone
200, and a second NOTE_STATUS_CHANGED audit row is written
409 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION, as the note is already archived
422, as ARCHIVED is not a valid target status for the route

items.explanation: After assertCanChangeStatus, updateStatus rejects a same-state change with 409 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION. Two concurrent archives that both read ACTIVE would still both write (finding F5).

items.prompt: A signed-in user creates a note whose title is two characters long (the minimum is three). What does the API return?

choices.text: 201, since titles are trimmed but never measured
500, since a zod error is not mapped by apiError
400 VALIDATION_ERROR with the raw zod error object
422 VALIDATION_ERROR with the flattened zod issues

choices: 201, since titles are trimmed but never measured
500, since a zod error is not mapped by apiError
400 VALIDATION_ERROR with the raw zod error object
422 VALIDATION_ERROR with the flattened zod issues

items.explanation: parseSchema uses safeParse and throws appError(..., 422, "VALIDATION_ERROR", result.error.flatten()), which apiError maps to its own status.

items.prompt: A script, not the browser form, POSTs to /api/notes/:id/share as the owner with the email " editor@notes.local" (one leading space) for an existing user. What comes back?

choices.text: 422 VALIDATION_ERROR, as the email check runs before trim
200, as the repository trims the address before lookup
404 USER_NOT_FOUND, as the stored email has no space
200, as the schema trims the address before it checks the format

choices: 422 VALIDATION_ERROR, as the email check runs before trim
200, as the repository trims the address before lookup
404 USER_NOT_FOUND, as the stored email has no space
200, as the schema trims the address before it checks the format

items.explanation: shareNoteSchema declares the email as z.email().trim().toLowerCase() (note-schemas.ts:27). In zod 4 those steps run in the order written, so the email-format check sees the raw value with its space and fails; trim and lowercase only apply to a value that already passed. A probe with zod 4.3.6 (the lockfile version) failed " dana@example.com" with invalid_format and accepted "Dana@Example.COM" as dana@example.com. parseSchema turns the failure into 422 VALIDATION_ERROR (parse-schema.ts:12-20) before the service runs (share/route.ts:25-26), so no lookup happens. The browser form avoids this only because an input of type email strips surrounding whitespace itself.

items.prompt: An editor saves a note whose currentVersionNumber is 3, and the save commits as version 4. Which message does the editor show right after the PUT returns 200?

choices.text: Saved version 4., as the hook refetches the note before the message
Saved version 4., as the response is read on the transaction client
A newer revision already exists, as the response looks out of date
Saved version 3., as the response is read outside the transaction

choices: Saved version 4., as the hook refetches the note before the message
Saved version 4., as the response is read on the transaction client
A newer revision already exists, as the response looks out of date
Saved version 3., as the response is read outside the transaction

items.explanation: updateNote runs the conditional update and the audit insert on the transaction client db, then returns noteRepository.findAccessibleById(...) from inside the callback (note-service.ts:263-293). That method takes no db argument and queries the global prisma client (note-repository.ts:103-108), so it runs on another pooled connection and, under PostgreSQL's default READ COMMITTED, cannot see the uncommitted update: it reads version 3. A probe with Prisma 6.19.3 (the lockfile version) on PostgreSQL 18 returned 3 through the global client and 4 through the transaction client inside the same callback. The workspace builds its message from that response (notes-workspace.tsx:196-209). A refetch shortly afterwards brings version 4 into the cache, but the message is already set; a 200 never enters the conflict branch.

items.prompt: A signed-in MEMBER who is not a collaborator requests GET /api/notes/<an existing note id>. What comes back?

choices.text: 200 with the note shown in a read-only view
403 FORBIDDEN, because the note exists but is not shared
404 NOTE_NOT_FOUND, the same as for a missing note
401 UNAUTHENTICATED, as the user lacks access

choices: 200 with the note shown in a read-only view
403 FORBIDDEN, because the note exists but is not shared
404 NOTE_NOT_FOUND, the same as for a missing note
401 UNAUTHENTICATED, as the user lacks access

items.explanation: findAccessibleById scopes members to notes where they have a collaborator row, so the note is not found and the service throws 404. The member cannot tell "not shared with me" from "does not exist".
